summary: Research Gregorian/neume references (Gregorio GABC, SMuFL chant assembly, music21, notationref) to ground a top-tier neume renderer

result.topic: Gregorio / GABC: Gregorian chant square-notation input format, neume engraving rules, and the do/fa clef system
result.keyFindings:
GABC is the de-facto text input format used by Gregorio/GregorioTeX to engrave Gregorian (square) chant notation. A GABC file is a header block of "field: value;" lines, a "%%" separator, then the score as a stream of "syllable(notes)" pairs; spaces between such pairs delimit words. Empty syllables hold standalone elements, e.g. "(c4)" for the initial clef or "(::)" for a bar. PITCH SYSTEM (relative to clef, NOT absolute note names). Pitches are single ASCII letters and denote a TYPOGRAPHIC STAFF POSITION, not a fixed note name. On the default 4-line staff the usable range is a..m (13 positions: a is lowest, m highest; adjacent letters = one diatonic step = one line-or-space). Letters do not "wrap" like modern note names — they are slot indices on the staff. Wider staves extend the range: 2-line a..i, 3-line a..k, 4-line a..m (default), 5-line a..n and p. Conventionally the staff is drawn so that a chosen middle slot (around g) sits in the middle of the staff. The ABSOLUTE solfege/pitch a given letter represents is determined entirely by the clef. Because the same letter = same staff slot regardless of clef, moving the clef reletters the music; this is the core "pitch is relative to clef" rule an implementer must honor: the renderer places a note at staff-slot(letter) and the SINGER derives solfege from clef position. CLEFS. Syntax: a clef token is the letter c (do clef) or f (fa clef), an OPTIONAL b for a clef-flat (e.g. cb3 = do-clef with a Bb), and a line number 1..(number of staff lines), counted from the BOTTOM line up. So legal do clefs are c1,c2,c3,c4 and fa clefs f1,f2,f3,f4 (c4 = do-clef on the 4th/top line is the most common). The do clef marks the line on which "do" (the tonic reference) is written; the fa clef marks the line on which "fa" sits. From that anchored line you read the diatonic scale up and down by line/space: e.g. for a do clef, the clef line = do, the space above = re, next line = mi, etc., descending = ti, la, sol below. The fa clef analogously anchors fa. Crucially there is NO fixed concert pitch in chant — clefs only fix the position of the semitones (mi-fa and ti-do) relative to the staff; the schola picks an absolute pitch. Two clefs may be typeset together (introduced v4.1) linked with @, e.g. c1@c4 / c4@f3. The clef can change mid-score by writing it in a new (clef) group; a custos is normally placed before a clef change. ACCIDENTALS. Appended after the pitch letter they affect: flat = x, natural = y, sharp = #. They behave like clef-flats — they apply to that pitch and remain in effect for the rest of the word (reset at the next bar/word), mirroring chant convention (notably the movable Bb). "Soft" variants exist: X soft flat, Y soft natural, ## soft sharp, printed only conditionally (soft flat shown only if no flat already in effect on that pitch; soft natural shown only if a flat/sharp is currently in effect; etc.). In GABC an accidental is written as its own note-letter+symbol, e.g. (gxg) puts a flat on the g. SINGLE NOTES / NOTE SHAPES (one letter + optional shape modifier): - lowercase a..m = punctum quadratum (the default square note). - UPPERCASE A..M = punctum inclinatum (diamond/oblique note), the descending-diamond shape used mainly inside a climacus. - v after the letter = virga (square note with a stem on the RIGHT), e.g. gv. V = virga reversa (stem on the LEFT). - o = oriscus (auto-chooses orientation); o0 forces it pointing down, o1 pointing up; O = oriscus scapus (oriscus with a stem). - w = quilisma (the zig-zag/wavy note), e.g. gw; appears as the middle/lower note of an ascending group. - s = stropha (apostropha). Repeating gives distropha (ss) and tristropha (sss): e.g. (gss), (gsss). - Inclinatum glyph can be forced with G0 (descending shape), G1 (ascending shape), G2 (punctum/unison shape). LIQUESCENCE (a note made smaller / curled to show a sung consonant). Modifiers attach after the pitch letter: - ~ = liquescent deminutus (the note is drawn small). Produces e.g. the cephalicus (descending liquescent of a clivis) and epiphonus (ascending liquescent of a pes) when applied to the upper note of those two-note neumes. - < = augmented (ascending) liquescence. - > = diminished (descending) liquescence. - - placed BEFORE the pitch (e.g. -g) = initio debilis (a weak/small starting note). RHYTHMIC / EXPRESSIVE MARKS (Solesmes signs), appended after the note: - . = punctum mora (the lengthening dot to the right of a note, "doubles" the note value). Multiple dots possible. For a clivis, attach both dots to the whole neume by writing them after the pair: prefer (fe..) over (f.e.) so the dots stay attached and don't get repositioned on export. - _ = horizontal episema (the small horizontal bar over/under a note indicating a slight broadening). Placement auto; can be tuned with numeric suffixes. - ' = vertical episema / ictus (the small vertical tick marking the rhythmic touch-point). '0 forces it below the note, '1 above. COMPOUND/COMPLEX NEUMES — built by simply CHAINING pitch letters with no separator; Gregorio auto-selects the correct ligature glyph from the melodic contour ("to any sequence of notes and spaces corresponds one and only one written form"). Notes are entered low-to-high in the order sung. Canonical primitives (using example pitches): - pes / podatus = two ASCENDING notes, e.g. (gh): drawn as a vertical two-note group, bottom note then upper note stacked/joined. - clivis / flexus = two DESCENDING notes, e.g. (hg) or (gf): first (higher) note with a descending stroke down to the second. - torculus = up-then-down (low-high-low), 3 notes e.g. (fgf) or (ghg): rises then falls. - porrectus = high-low-high (down-then-up), 3 notes e.g. (gfg): engraved with the characteristic thick CURVED swoosh stroke connecting the first descending pair, then the final ascending note. (Technically a torculus resupinus form.) - scandicus = three or more ASCENDING notes, e.g. (fgh): a rising series, typically punctum + pes or stacked ascending notes, often topping with a virga. - climacus = a high note followed by DESCENDING puncta inclinata, written as the first note then UPPERCASE letters for the diamonds, e.g. (gFE) = note g then descending diamonds f, e. This is the canonical use of uppercase letters. - distropha (ss) / tristropha (sss) = 2 / 3 repeated strophae on the same pitch, e.g. (gss),(gsss). - pressus = two notes at the same pitch fused (an oriscus/note + note), shown as a thickened repeated-pitch figure; built from oriscus + following note. - salicus = ascending 3-note group whose MIDDLE note is an oriscus (e.g. (foh) style) and which carries an ictus on that oriscus — distinct from a scandicus by the oriscus + vertical episema. - virga strata = a note followed by an oriscus forming a specific ascending two-note figure. Liquescent versions of any of the above come from adding ~ / < / > to the relevant (usually final) note; auctum (lengthened) and deminutum (shrunk) forms are these liquescent/episema variants. Fusion of notes into a single glyph (e.g. for special ligatures) uses @ between notes; q gives a pes quadratum (square-topped pes) by placing the second note to the right of the connecting bar. SPACES (control horizontal gaps; some keep notes in the SAME neume, some separate neumes): - ! = zero-width neumatic break (no added space but breaks the ligature so following notes are a new glyph) — used to split what would auto-fuse. - /! = a very small separation, still within the same neume. - /0 = a half/zero space, part of the same neume. - / = small neumatic cut (separation between neumes within a syllable). - // = larger/medium neumatic cut. - /[n] or /factor = a custom-scaled space. - a plain space inside (...) is generally not used; spacing is via these tokens, and word spacing comes from the space between syllable(...) groups. DIVISIONES (bar lines / breath marks), each written as its own (token) group between syllables: - ` (backtick) = virgula (the smallest breath tick). - , = divisio minima (quarter bar; short stroke through the top space). - ; = divisio minor (half bar; stroke through upper half of staff). Variants ;1.. for height. - : = divisio maior (full bar through the whole staff). - :: = divisio finalis (the double full bar ending a piece/section). CUSTOS (the small guide mark at the END of a line/staff showing the pitch of the first note on the NEXT line). Gregorio inserts custodes AUTOMATICALLY at line breaks by default. Manual control: z0 forces/handles a custos at a clef change; a pitched custos is written as a note letter followed by + (e.g. g+). Custodes are normally emitted just before a clef change or line end. TEXT / SYLLABLE layer (relevant because notes bind to syllables): format is syllable(notes); the first vowel/center of the syllable aligns under the neume's center. Markup tags: italic, bold,
    underline, colored, small caps, ... special glyphs (e.g. R/ for the response sign, ae ligature), and {..} marks the manual centering point. Header block: only name: is mandatory; other common fields are office-part, mode, commentary, annotation, etc.; the block ends with %% on its own line.
actionable: Model a Note as {staffSlot:int, shape:enum} where staffSlot comes from mapping letters a..m to 0..12 (a=bottom). Render by placing the glyph at line/space = staffSlot; do NOT store absolute note names — pitch identity is derived only when you also know the active clef.
Implement clef as {type: do|fa, hasFlat:bool, line:int(1..staffLines)}. Parse the token regex: ^([cf])(b?)([1-9])$ ; line is counted from the bottom line. Default staff = 4 lines, range a..m.

Derive solfege/absolute pitch for display by anchoring: for a do-clef, the clef's line slot = 'do'; for an fa-clef the clef's line slot = 'fa'; then walk the diatonic scale up/down per staff slot, placing semitones at mi-fa and ti-do. This is needed only for audio/transposition, not for drawing.

Support clef-flat (cb3/fb3) and inline accidentals x(flat) y(natural) #(sharp) appended to a pitch letter; make accidentals persist until the next divisio/word, then reset — matching the movable-Bb convention.

Build a neume tokenizer that, inside each (...), reads: optional leading '-' (initio debilis), a pitch letter (lower=punctum, UPPER=punctum inclinatum), then zero+ shape/modifier chars: v/V (virga/reversa), o/o0/o1/O (oriscus), w (quilisma), s/ss/sss (stropha/di/tristropha), ~ (deminutus), < (augmentum), > (deminutum-liquescent), _ (episema), . (mora, repeatable), ' / '0 / '1 (ictus), and accidentals x/y/#.

Auto-select compound-neume glyphs from melodic contour of chained letters rather than requiring explicit neume names: 2 up=pes, 2 down=clivis, up-down=torculus, down-up=porrectus(curved stroke), 3+ up=scandicus, note+UPPERCASE descending=climacus. Enforce the invariant 'one note sequence -> one glyph'.

Render the porrectus with the special thick curved (swoosh) stroke for the descending first interval; render climacus tails as descending diamonds (puncta inclinata); render quilisma as the wavy glyph and only as a rising-group middle note.

Implement liquescence by shrinking the affected (usually final) note glyph: ~ small deminutus, < ascending-curl, > descending-curl; this yields cephalicus (clivis+~) and epiphonus (pes+~) automatically.

Implement spacing tokens as glue widths between glyphs: ! zero-width-but-break, /! tiny, /0 half, / small, // medium, /[n] scaled; keep '!','/!','/0' as intra-neume (same group) and '/','//'  as inter-neume.
Implement divisiones as their own glyphs spanning defined staff heights: ` virgula, , minima (top space), ; minor (upper half), : maior (full), :: finalis (double full).
Auto-emit a custos at every line break showing the pitch of the next line's first note; support manual pitched custos 'letter+' and z0 at clef changes.

Parse the file as: header lines 'field: value;' until a line that is exactly '%%', then a stream of syllableText(noteString) tokens with whitespace as the word separator; treat empty-text groups like (c4) and (::) as standalone clef/bar elements.
gotchas: Letters are STAFF POSITIONS, not note names — they never wrap (no octave repeat). a..m are 13 ordered slots; a renderer that treats them as pitch classes will be wrong. Absolute pitch only exists relative to the clef.
Clef line numbers count from the BOTTOM line up, and the count maxes at the number of staff lines (4 by default), so f4/c4 are valid but c5 is only valid on a 5-line staff.

Same uppercase letters mean two different things by context: A..M are puncta inclinata (note shapes), while clef/bar tokens and accidentals use other letters (c,f,b,x,y) — disambiguate by position (clef/accidental vs. standalone note).
Climacus is the ONLY common place uppercase (inclinatum) letters appear; do not auto-uppercase descending notes elsewhere or you will mis-engrave.
Mora-dot placement on multi-note neumes is fragile: attach dots to the whole neume (e.g. fe.. not f.e.) or PDF/layout passes may reposition them. Decide dot binding at the neume level.

The fa clef vs do clef difference is purely WHERE the semitone pattern lands; there is no fixed reference pitch in chant. Do not hardcode A440-style absolute pitches; transposition is free for the schola.
Accidentals (esp. flat on b) are local: they persist only to the next bar/word, not the whole piece, unlike modern key signatures. Clef-flats (cb/fb) are the closest thing to a key signature.

Quilisma (w), oriscus (o/O), pressus and salicus are easy to confuse: salicus = ascending group whose middle note is an oriscus PLUS an ictus; pressus = repeated/fused same-pitch via oriscus+note. Distinguish by the presence of the oriscus glyph and the ictus.
Spaces are semantically split into intra-neume (!, /!, /0) vs inter-neume (/, //) — using the wrong class changes whether Gregorio fuses notes into one glyph.

GABC has dialect/version drift (docs reference v4.1, v5.x); some tokens (double clefs @, soft accidentals X/Y/##, G0/G1/G2 inclinatum forcing) were added in specific versions — pin to a target Gregorio version when claiming full fidelity.
Liquescent direction tokens <, > also look like XML/markup angle brackets used in the TEXT layer; parse note-modifiers only inside (...) note context to avoid collisions with <i>, <sp>, etc.

The PDF guide source was image-only and could not be parsed; the do/fa-to-solfege reading rule is corroborated by standard Solesmes/Liber Usualis theory plus the Gregorio docs, not a single fetched verbatim page — verify against an official Gregorio neume table before final implementation.

result.topic: Assembling Gregorian neumes from SMuFL chant glyph components (SMuFL latest "Medieval and Renaissance plainchant" ranges) for a Flutter/Canvas renderer
result.keyFindings:
COORDINATE SYSTEM AND UNITS. SMuFL describes everything in staff spaces (sp). In a standard 5-line context 1 sp = 0.25 em; the bundled Bravura `glyphBBoxes`/`glyphAdvanceWidths` values are already expressed in staff spaces (so "0.64" means 0.64 sp wide). Every glyph's origin is at baseline-left (x=0 at left sidebearing reference, y=0 at the SMuFL baseline). y increases UPWARD. To draw in a Flutter Canvas (y-down), negate the y of every SW/NE/offset and flip with a transform, or compute positions in sp then map sp->px with a single scale and y-inversion. `advanceWidth` is the horizontal pen advance after drawing a glyph; it differs from bbox width and is the number you use to lay glyphs left-to-right.

CHANT STAFF (the canvas the rest registers against). chantStaff U+E8F0 (W=2.0 sp), chantStaffNarrow U+E8F2 (W=1.0), chantStaffWide U+E8F1 (W=3.0); all have bbox SW.y=-1.532, NE.y=+1.532 (H=3.064 sp), symmetric about the origin y=0. The chant staff is a FOUR-LINE staff. The four lines sit symmetric about y=0; outer lines at roughly +-1.532 sp, giving an inter-LINE gap of ~1.02 sp. Critically, one DIATONIC STEP (a note moving from a line to the adjacent space, or space to line) = HALF that gap ~= 0.5 sp. So: staffPosToY(step) = step * (lineGap/2), with lineGap derived from your chosen staff (use the metadata: lineGap = 3.064/3 if you treat the bbox extremes as the outer lines, or simply pick a clean value like 1.0 sp per line / 0.5 sp per diatonic step and scale the whole system). You build a continuous staff by TILING the staff glyph horizontally: repeat chantStaff at x += advanceWidth(chantStaff)=2.0 sp until the desired width, or draw chantStaffWide/Narrow to fill remainders. The staff glyph carries its own 4 lines; you do not draw lines manually.

CLEFS DEFINE PITCH (do-clef / C-clef). chantCclef U+E906 (the movable "do" clef; bbox H=1.768, adv 0.536) and chantFclef U+E902 (the "fa" clef; bbox H=1.808, adv 1.056). In chant the clef is positioned ON a chosen staff line; that line is then DO (for the C-clef) or FA (for the F-clef). The clef's vertical origin (y=0) is its reference point: place the clef so its reference sits on the target line, i.e. translate the clef by staffPosToY(lineIndex). All subsequent neume vertical positions are computed as diatonic offsets from that clef-defined reference pitch: pitchToStep(pitch) relative to the clef line, then staffPosToY(step). Because chant has no fixed absolute pitch, the clef ONLY establishes the relative position of DO/FA on the staff; your model maps a logical pitch (e.g. letter+octave or a scale-degree) to a diatonic step count from the clef line and multiplies by half-the-line-gap. Hufnagel stylistic alternates exist (chantCclefHufnagel, chantFclefHufnagel) for German notation but are the optional `ss0x` set glyphs.

SINGLE-NOTE BUILDING BLOCKS (range U+E990-U+E9A1). chantPunctum U+E990 (W=0.64, adv 0.64; SW=(0,-0.404) NE=(0.64,0.408) -> vertically centered on its origin, so origin y=0 is the note center). chantPunctumInclinatum U+E991 (diamond, adv 0.6; used for the descending notes of a climacus). chantPunctumVirga U+E996 / chantPunctumVirgaReversed U+E997 (W=0.64, adv 0.64; bbox SW.y=-1.604 NE.y=+0.408 -> the punctum head is centered on origin like the punctum, and a STEM hangs DOWN ~1.6 sp below; "reversed" mirrors stem side). chantQuilisma U+E99B, chantOriscusAscending/Descending/Liquescens U+E99C-E, chantStrophicus/StrophicusAuctus U+E99F-A0. These are all "note-like" and are positioned exactly like a notehead: translate vertically by staffPosToY(step) so the glyph's origin (note center) lands on the target line/space.

CONNECTING / ENTRY / LIGATURA LINES are the JOINERS that turn single notes into compound neumes (range U+E9B0-E9C5). Three families:
1) chantConnectingLineAsc2nd-6th (U+E9BD-E9C1): thin vertical connector, W=0.056 sp. Geometry: SW.y=-0.6 always (origin sits 0.6 sp above the BOTTOM of the line); NE.y = 0.6 + 0.6*(N-1) for the Nth, i.e. heights 1.2/1.8/2.4/3.0/3.6 sp for 2nd/3rd/4th/5th/6th. Each additional interval index adds exactly 0.6 sp. EDITORIAL RULE (verbatim from SMuFL): "the connecting lines (e.g. chantConnectingLineAsc3rd) should likewise be positioned on the staff line or space corresponding to the bottom of the line." So you register the connecting line at the LOWER (starting) pitch.
2) chantEntryLineAsc2nd-6th (U+E9B4-E9B8): same width 0.056 and same height series (1.2..3.6, SW.y=-0.6) - a lead-IN stroke approaching a note from below (used at the start of a neume or to attach an entry stroke); positioned by its bottom like the connecting line.
3) chantLigaturaDesc2nd-5th (U+E9B9-E9BC): a thick DESCENDING ligated stroke that already contains both note-bodies fused (W=1.86 for 2nd up to 2.316 for 3rd-5th; heights grow downward, SW.y goes -0.912/-1.6/-2.212/-2.812, NE.y=+0.416). EDITORIAL RULE (verbatim): "Glyphs should be positioned relative to their starting pitch: for example, the chantLigaturaDesc3rd glyph, which describes a downwards progression by an interval of a third, should be positioned on the staff line or space of the starting note of the downwards pattern." So a ligatura is registered at the TOP (first/higher) note and the glyph itself draws down to the lower note.

THE PODATUS/PES KEYSTONE (the canonical worked example for 2-note ascending). chantPodatusLower U+E9B0 (SW=(0,0) NE=(0.616,0.656), adv 0.556) draws the LOWER note plus an ascending stem rising to the right; its origin y=0 is the bottom (lower-note baseline). chantPodatusUpper U+E9B1 (SW=(-0.508,-0.012) NE=(0.056,0.780), advanceWidth=0.0) draws the UPPER note; it has NEGATIVE x extent and ZERO advance so it is meant to be OVERPRINTED on top of the lower glyph: after drawing chantPodatusLower you do NOT advance the pen (or you back up), translate UP by the interval in staff positions, then draw chantPodatusUpper at the same x. For a podatus larger than a 2nd you insert a connecting line: SMuFL's documented recipe = chantPodatusLower + chantConnectingLineAsc(Nth) raising the second note by N, + chantPodatusUpper at the raised position. For a plain 2nd the two podatus halves abut directly with no connecting line.

LIQUESCENT ASSEMBLY (verbatim editorial rule): "for an ascending liquescent, position chantAuctumAsc on the starting staff position, and chantDeminutumUpper on the ending staff position, with the appropriate length of connecting line between them." chantAuctumAsc U+E994 / chantAuctumDesc U+E995 are the auctum (growing) note bodies; chantDeminutumUpper U+E9B2 / chantDeminutumLower U+E9B3 are the small terminal liquescent notes (note their bbox has NEGATIVE x like the podatus upper: SW.x=-0.248, adv 0.056 -> they overprint/attach to the end of a connecting line). General app rule (verbatim): "Scoring applications should position these glyphs like any other notehead, i.e. moving them vertically according to the desired starting staff position."

ARTICULATIONS / RHYTHMIC SIGNS (range U+E9D0-E9D9), all positioned relative to a target note's center (origin y=0) and centered horizontally over/under it:
- chantEpisema U+E9D8: a short horizontal bar (W=0.704, H=0.08; bbox y 0.50..0.58 -> drawn ~0.5 sp ABOVE the note origin by default). It marks a lengthened/stressed note; center it horizontally over the note (offset x by (noteWidth - episemaWidth)/2) and raise/lower so it clears the note. For an episema BELOW, mirror its y.
- chantAugmentum U+E9D9 (the mora dot / "Augmentum (mora)"): a dot (W=0.264, bbox y 0.20..0.456) placed AFTER a note to double its value; position it to the right of the note (x += note advance) at the same staff position (often nudged into the adjacent space). 
- chantIctusAbove U+E9D0 / chantIctusBelow U+E9D1: short vertical stroke (W=0.128, H=0.424); the rhythmic ictus, placed centered above (y ~0.11..0.54) or below (y -0.54..-0.11) the note.
- chantAccentusAbove/Below U+E9D6/7, chantCirculusAbove/Below U+E9D2/3, chantSemicirculusAbove/Below U+E9D4/5: ancient performance signs, each with an Above (positive y) and Below (negative y) variant; place centered over/under the note, choosing the variant by desired side.

DIVISIONS / BREATH MARKS (range U+E8F3-E8F8, on the staff between syllables/phrases). chantDivisioMinima U+E8F3 (short stroke through the top space; bbox y 1.0..2.0), chantDivisioMaior U+E8F4 (half-staff bar, y -1.0..1.0), chantDivisioMaxima U+E8F5 (full-height bar, y -1.5..1.5), chantDivisioFinalis U+E8F6 (double thick+thin final bar, W=0.48), chantVirgula U+E8F7 (tiny tick at top, y 1.02..2.0), chantCaesura U+E8F8 (y 1.04..2.0). These are drawn at a fixed vertical registration spanning the staff (their bboxes already encode the height), placed inline at the x where the division falls.

CUSTOS (end-of-line guide pointing to the next system's first pitch), range U+EA04-EA09: chantCustosStemUpPosLowest/Low/Middle (U+EA04-06) and chantCustosStemDownPosMiddle/High/Highest (U+EA07-09). Choose UP vs DOWN stem and the Pos variant by where the next pitch is, then translate vertically by staffPosToY(nextPitchStep) and place at the right edge of the line. The custos head registers at the target pitch.

CONCRETE ASSEMBLY RECIPES (origin convention: place the FIRST note's center at the clef-derived y for its pitch; advance x by each glyph's advanceWidth unless noted; raise(N) = translate up by N diatonic steps = staffPosToY delta; a 2nd uses the smallest connecting/entry segment):
- PUNCTUM (1 note): draw chantPunctum at (x, y(p1)). 
- VIRGA (1 note, higher in a context): draw chantPunctumVirga at (x, y(p1)) (stem hangs below the head).
- PES / PODATUS (2 notes ascending p1<p2): draw chantPodatusLower at (x, y(p1)); if interval>2nd insert chantConnectingLineAsc(interval) registered at its bottom = y(p1); then draw chantPodatusUpper WITHOUT advancing (advance=0), translated to y(p2). (Alternative generic build: chantPunctum at y(p1) + chantConnectingLineAsc(N) bottom at y(p1) + chantPunctumVirga or chantPunctum at y(p2).)
- CLIVIS (2 notes descending p1>p2): use a descending ligature - draw chantLigaturaDesc(interval) registered at the STARTING (higher) note y(p1); the single glyph renders both notes down to p2. (Generic alternative: virga at y(p1) + chantPunctum at y(p2) joined by a thin descending stroke / right-side stem.)
- TORCULUS (3 notes: p1 up to p2 down to p3, low-high-low): chantPunctum at y(p1) + chantConnectingLineAsc(p1->p2) bottom at y(p1) + middle note at y(p2), then chantLigaturaDesc(p2->p3) registered at y(p2) for the descent to p3. (i.e. an ascending join followed by a descending ligature sharing the apex note.)
- PORRECTUS (3 notes: p1 down to p2 up to p3, high-low-high): chantLigaturaDesc(p1->p2) registered at y(p1) for the opening descent (in real chant the first two notes are the thick slanted porrectus stroke), then chantConnectingLineAsc(p2->p3) bottom at y(p2) + final note (chantPunctumVirga) at y(p3).
- SCANDICUS (3 notes ascending p1<p2<p3): stack two ascending steps - chantPunctum at y(p1); chantConnectingLineAsc(p1->p2) bottom y(p1) + chantPunctum at y(p2); chantConnectingLineAsc(p2->p3) bottom y(p2) + chantPunctumVirga at y(p3) (top note as virga). Effectively podatus-on-podatus; for the lowest two notes you may use chantEntryLineAsc(N) as the lead-in stroke.
- CLIMACUS (3+ notes descending p1>p2>p3...): chantPunctumVirga at y(p1) for the first (highest) note, then a series of chantPunctumInclinatum (diamond) glyphs each placed lower at y(p2), y(p3)... stepping down and to the right by each glyph's advance (no connecting line; the inclinatum diamonds are the descending tail). 
- Longer compounds (torculus resupinus, porrectus flexus, scandicus flexus, climacus resupinus) are concatenations of the above primitives sharing the boundary note.

PER-INTERVAL VERTICAL MATH. To place the raised note of any ascending join: deltaY = (intervalNumber-1) * diatonicStep where diatonicStep ~= 0.5 sp (half the chant line gap). The connecting/entry/ligatura glyph for that interval has matching height (2nd=1.2, +0.6 per step), so picking glyph by interval number automatically gives the right reach; you only need to translate the upper glyph by deltaY and the line glyph is placed by its bottom at the lower note.
actionable: Build a sp->px mapping helper: 1 staff space = scale unit, y inverted for Canvas. Read all chant glyph metrics from the already-bundled assets/smufl/bravura_metadata.json (glyphBBoxes + glyphAdvanceWidths) rather than hardcoding - the bbox SW/NE in staff spaces is the single source of truth for registration.

Implement staffPosToY(diatonicStep) = diatonicStep * (lineGap/2). Derive lineGap from chantStaff bbox (H=3.064 sp over the 4 lines) or pick a clean lineGap (e.g. 1.0 sp -> 0.5 sp per diatonic step) and scale the whole system uniformly.

Render the staff by tiling chantStaff (U+E8F0, advanceWidth 2.0 sp) horizontally to the needed width, filling remainders with chantStaffWide (3.0) / chantStaffNarrow (1.0). Do not hand-draw staff lines; the glyph contains its 4 lines centered on y=0.

Place clefs by their origin: chantCclef (U+E906) reference y=0 -> translate by staffPosToY(clefLineStep) so that line becomes DO; chantFclef (U+E902) likewise for FA. Compute every neume pitch as a diatonic step offset from the clef line, never as an absolute pitch.

Treat every single-note glyph (chantPunctum E990, chantPunctumVirga E996, chantQuilisma E99B, oriscus/strophicus) as a notehead whose origin y=0 is the note center; position with translate(x, staffPosToY(step)) then advance x by advanceWidth.

Implement the PES/PODATUS as the keystone: draw chantPodatusLower (E9B0, origin at lower-note bottom SW=(0,0)) then draw chantPodatusUpper (E9B1, advanceWidth 0, negative-x bbox) at the SAME x translated up to the upper pitch; insert chantConnectingLineAsc(N) (E9BD..E9C1) registered at its BOTTOM = lower note y when interval > a 2nd.

Select connecting/entry/ligatura glyph purely by interval number: chantConnectingLineAsc2nd..6th and chantEntryLineAsc2nd..6th (heights 1.2/1.8/2.4/3.0/3.6 sp, +0.6 per step) for ascending joins registered at the bottom note; chantLigaturaDesc2nd..5th for descending joins registered at the TOP (starting) note.

Build compound neumes by concatenating primitives sharing the boundary note per the recipes: scandicus = podatus stacked; climacus = chantPunctumVirga then a run of chantPunctumInclinatum (E991) stepping down by each glyph's advance; torculus = ascending join + descending ligatura at the apex; porrectus = descending ligatura + ascending join at the valley.

Assemble liquescents per the spec: ascending = chantAuctumAsc (E994) at start pitch + chantDeminutumUpper (E9B2) at end pitch + connecting line of the matching interval between them (deminutum glyphs have advance 0 / negative-x and overprint the line end).

Attach articulations centered on the target note's origin: chantEpisema (E9D8) horizontal bar centered over the note (x offset = (noteWidth-0.704)/2, raise above note); chantAugmentum mora dot (E9D9) to the RIGHT of the note (x += note advance); chantIctusAbove/Below (E9D0/1) and accentus/circulus/semicirculus Above/Below variants picked by desired side, centered horizontally.

Place divisiones (E8F3-E8F8) inline between syllables at a fixed staff-spanning vertical registration taken from their bbox (minima top-space, maior half-bar, maxima full bar, finalis double bar). Place custos (EA04-EA09) at line end, choosing stem-up/down + Pos variant and translating its head to the next system's first pitch.

Extend the existing NcForm/NeumeType model in lib/core/neume.dart with a GLYPH-MAPPING layer (NcForm/NeumeType -> SMuFL codepoint(s) + connector selection) and create a new chant renderer under lib/src (none exists today) that consumes Neume/NeumeComponent and emits positioned glyph draw calls using the recipes above.
gotchas: Chant glyphs carry NO anchors and NO ligature entries in Bravura's metadata (verified: glyphsWithAnchors has 0 chant entries, ligatures has 0). All assembly is GEOMETRIC via baseline registration + bbox/advance math - you cannot rely on cutOutN/anchor points like for CMN stems/flags.

chantPodatusUpper, chantDeminutumUpper, chantDeminutumLower have advanceWidth=0 and NEGATIVE x bbox (e.g. PodatusUpper SW.x=-0.508). They are OVERPRINT glyphs: if you blindly advance the pen by advanceWidth or place them at the next x slot they will render in the wrong place. You must keep the same x as the partner glyph and only translate vertically.

A diatonic STEP on the chant staff is HALF the inter-line gap (line<->adjacent space), ~0.5 sp, NOT a full line gap. Off-by-2x vertical errors are the most likely bug. The connecting-line glyph height grows 0.6 sp per interval index, which is slightly more than the pure pitch delta (it overshoots to overlap the noteheads) - register the line by its bottom and let it overshoot; do not try to make line height equal pitch delta exactly.

Ascending joiners (connecting/entry lines) are registered at the BOTTOM/STARTING note; descending ligatura strokes are registered at the TOP/STARTING note. Mixing these two registration conventions is an easy mistake - the SMuFL editorial text explicitly distinguishes them.

The SMuFL spec site does a host-level redirect from w3c.github.io to w3c-cg.github.io and many old table/specification page URLs 404. The live editorial guidance lives at w3c-cg.github.io/.../tables/medieval-and-renaissance-plainchant-multiple-note-forms.html. Don't trust stale w3c.github.io deep links.

GB metadata bbox y-values are baseline-up; Flutter Canvas is y-down. Every y from the metadata must be negated/flipped. The punctum is vertically centered on its origin (SW.y=-0.404, NE.y=+0.408) so origin=note center, but the podatus lower has origin at its BOTTOM (SW.y=0) - the origin convention is NOT uniform across glyphs, so always read each glyph's bbox rather than assuming center-registration.

Hufnagel clef/note variants (chantCclefHufnagel etc.) are optionalGlyphs / stylistic set glyphs, not in the main cmap mapping the same way - only use them if you explicitly need German Hufnagel style, and they have very different widths (Cclef 0.536 vs Hufnagel 1.144).

chant does not have absolute pitch - the C/F clef only fixes the relative position of DO/FA. Modeling neume pitches as absolute MIDI/letter pitches will fight the notation; model them as diatonic steps relative to the clef line.

There is currently NO chant renderer in lib/src (grep found zero chant/neume rendering code there); only the data model in lib/core/neume.dart exists. This is a from-scratch renderer, so the recipes here are the spec, not something to reconcile against existing rendering code.

The ligatura glyphs (Desc2nd-5th) are FUSED two-note shapes, not joiners between two separately-drawn notes. For a clivis you draw ONE ligatura glyph, not punctum+line+punctum. Conversely the ascending connecting lines ARE thin joiners between two separately-drawn notes. Don't apply one model to both.

result.topic: Using music21 (and chant21) as an external validator for flutter_notemus output — modern CMN and Gregorian/medieval chant
result.keyFindings:
VERIFIED IN THIS ENVIRONMENT: Python 3.13.13 with music21 10.3.0 is already installed (chant21 is NOT). All smoke tests below were run live against this install.

(1) DOES music21 REPRESENT NEUMES / GREGORIAN CHANT, AND CAN IT PARSE A CHANT FORMAT?
- Core music21 has a `music21.volpiano` module that round-trips Volpiano (the CANTUS-database plainchant font) <-> music21 Streams. It produces ordinary `note.Note` objects, embeds clefs/flats/naturals, marks liquescence in note.editorial, and groups multi-note neumes as `volpiano.Neume` Spanner objects (plus LineBreak/PageBreak/ColumnBreak classes). Live test: `volpiano.toPart("1---c-d-e-f-g-h---4")` yielded 6 notes. The module docstring still says it "will move to a medren package hopefully by v7" — that medren package never fully materialized; there is no general-purpose `music21.medren`/neume-shape module in 10.x. So music21 models chant pitches as ordinary notes on a staff, NOT as neume SHAPES (punctum/virga/quilisma/pes/clivis/torculus etc.). It cannot represent the graphical neume vocabulary that flutter_notemus models in lib/core/neume.dart.
- GABC: music21 has NO native GABC parser. The bridge is the third-party library chant21 (bacor/chant21, MIT, last pushed 2024-09). chant21 registers SubConverters into music21.converter for BOTH gabc and Volpiano. Verified from source chant21/gabc/converter.py: `class ConverterGABC(converter.subConverters.SubConverter)` with `registerFormats = ('gabc','GABC')`, `registerInputExtensions = ('gabc','GABC')`, and module import calls `converter.registerSubconverter(ConverterGABC)`. So after `import chant21`, you can do `converter.parse(gabcString, format='gabc')` or parse a .gabc file by extension. chant21 preserves the full chant hierarchy (sections, words, syllables, neumes) as music21 subclasses (chant.Note etc.), and ships GregoBaseCorpus (~9000 gabc transcriptions) and CantusCorpus (~60000 Volpiano melodies) loaders. chant21 deps: music21>=5.7.2, Arpeggio (PEG parser), Jinja2, PyYAML==5.3.1; python_requires>=3.7. Because it pins only music21>=5.7.2 and was last touched in the v5/v6 era, it is NOT guaranteed to import cleanly under music21 10.3.0 — must be tested before relying on it (the strict PyYAML==5.3.1 pin in particular can conflict on Python 3.13).

(2) WHICH music21 FEATURES ARE USABLE TO VALIDATE flutter_notemus OUTPUT (modern CMN):
flutter_notemus already emits MusicXML. VERIFIED in repo: lib/src/parsers/musicxml_parser.dart has `MusicXMLParser.staffToMusicXML(Staff)` which builds a `<score-partwise>` version 4.0 document (emits part-list, part, measure, attributes/clef/key/time, notes), plus `mergeStaffs`, `validateMusicXML`, `extractMetadata`, `convertPartwiseToTimewise`. This class is part of the public API (exported from lib/flutter_notemus.dart line 55). That MusicXML string is exactly what you feed to music21.
Usable music21 validators (all confirmed working on 10.3.0):
- `converter.parse(xmlString)` / `converter.parseData(...)` ingests MusicXML and returns a Score/Part. (Round-trip verified: parsed tinyNotation, wrote MusicXML, reparsed — 1 measure preserved.)
- `stream.isWellFormedNotation()` -> bool: asserts Score contains Parts containing Measures. Returned True on a valid parse.
- `stream.makeNotation()` rebuilds measures/beams/accidentals and warns/throws on notation that cannot be expressed — a good "does this survive engraving normalization" gate.
- Measure-duration vs time-signature checking: `Measure.barDuration.quarterLength` vs `Measure.highestTime`. Live test detected a 3-beat measure under a 4/4 signature (highestTime 3.0 vs barDuration 4.0). This is the core "do note durations sum to the meter" assertion.
- Pitch/accidental validation: `note.pitch.midi`, `.nameWithOctave`, enharmonic/spelling; chord building; range checks.
- Key/meter inference for cross-checks: `stream.analyze('key')` (returned "d minor" on a test), and `getElementsByClass(meter.TimeSignature)` to assert the meter you exported is what landed.
- Counting/structure assertions: number of measures, notes (`recurse().notes`), parts, ties, tuplets, lyrics (`note.lyrics`), clefs, key signatures — everything to assert "what I exported is what music21 read back".
- music21 also imports MEI (`music21.mei`) and many other formats, useful if you later add an MEI exporter for CMN.

(3) CONCRETE PLAN — music21 as an external validator in this repo:
Pipeline: flutter_notemus Score -> MusicXMLParser.staffToMusicXML -> .musicxml file -> python validator (music21) -> JSON pass/fail -> Dart test asserts.
Step A (modern CMN, do this first — highest value, lowest risk):
  1. Add a Dart test/CLI that builds representative Scores and writes their staffToMusicXML output to test/golden/*.musicxml (or a temp dir).
  2. Add tool/validate_musicxml.py: `from music21 import converter; s = converter.parse(sys.argv[1])`; then assert `s.isWellFormedNotation()`; run `s.makeNotation()`; for each measure assert `m.barDuration.quarterLength == m.highestTime` (allowing intentional anacrusis/pickup); compare note count, pitches (nameWithOctave list), durations (quarterLength list), time signatures, key signatures against an expected JSON the Dart side emits alongside the XML. Print a JSON {ok, errors[]} and exit nonzero on failure.
  3. Drive it from CI: a small bootstrap that does `pip install music21` then runs the Dart export step and the python validator; fail the build on nonzero exit. Optionally invoke python from a Dart integration test via Process.run for a single `flutter test`-able gate.
Step B (chant — optional, lower confidence):
  - music21 cannot validate flutter_notemus's NEUME SHAPES. What it CAN validate is the underlying pitch/melodic content if flutter_notemus can also emit GABC or Volpiano (or you author the chant in GABC and treat flutter_notemus as the renderer). Plan: keep canonical chant test inputs as .gabc; in python do `import chant21; from music21 import converter; c = converter.parse(open('x.gabc').read(), format='gabc')` and assert the parsed pitch sequence / syllable-to-note mapping matches what flutter_notemus rendered. This validates pitches, text underlay, section/word/syllable/neume grouping COUNTS — not glyph correctness. Gate this behind a feature flag and pin chant21 in a dedicated venv because of its old deps.

LIMITS (be honest): music21 is a pitch/duration/analysis toolkit, not a neume-glyph or square-notation validator. It does NOT know punctum vs virga vs quilisma, ligature shapes, episema, mode/psalm-tone correctness, custos, or square-notation clef-on-4-line-staff conventions — exactly the things flutter_notemus's neume.dart/mensural.dart model. music21's MEI IMPORT explicitly does NOT support mensural or neume/chant notation (documented limitation), and MEI EXPORT is not implemented at all — so an MEI-based chant validation path is a dead end today. For chant, music21+chant21 can only assert the reduced "notes-on-a-staff + text + structural grouping" view, and chant21's age/dependency pins make its compatibility with music21 10.3.0 something you must verify, not assume.
actionable: Add tool/validate_musicxml.py that runs music21: converter.parse(xml) -> assert isWellFormedNotation() -> makeNotation() -> per-measure assert Measure.barDuration.quarterLength == Measure.highestTime (allow declared anacrusis) -> compare note pitches/durations/time-sigs/key-sigs/counts against an expected JSON; print {ok,errors[]} and exit nonzero on failure.

Reuse the EXISTING exporter: MusicXMLParser.staffToMusicXML(Staff) in lib/src/parsers/musicxml_parser.dart already emits <score-partwise> v4.0 and is public API (lib/flutter_notemus.dart). No new exporter needed for the CMN validation path.

Have the Dart side write paired artifacts per fixture: a .musicxml file AND an expected.json (pitch list as nameWithOctave, durations as quarterLength, time signatures, key, measure/note counts) so the python validator does a deterministic diff, not just a parse-smoke-test.

Wire a CI job (and/or a Dart integration test using Process.run) that does `pip install music21`, exports the fixtures, runs the validator, and fails the build on nonzero exit. music21 10.3.0 is already present locally, so local runs need no setup.
For the measure-duration check, special-case pickup/anacrusis and final/short measures (use Measure.paddingLeft/paddingRight or an expected-incomplete flag) to avoid false positives.
Add round-trip regression coverage: parse flutter_notemus MusicXML with music21, re-serialize via s.write('musicxml'), reparse, and assert pitch/duration stability — catches lossy export bugs.

For chant: keep canonical test melodies as .gabc files; in a SEPARATE pinned venv run `import chant21; converter.parse(gabc, format='gabc')` and assert the pitch sequence + syllable/word/section/neume grouping COUNTS match flutter_notemus's rendered model. Treat this as melodic/text validation only, never glyph validation.

Before adopting chant21, run a compatibility spike: `pip install chant21` in an isolated venv and confirm it imports and parses a sample .gabc under music21 10.3.0 (its deps pin PyYAML==5.3.1 and target music21>=5.7.2 from the v5/v6 era).

Document explicitly in the repo that music21 validates pitch/duration/meter/key/structure only — neume shapes, ligatures, episema, mode/psalm-tone, custos, and square-notation engraving in lib/core/neume.dart and lib/core/mensural.dart are OUT OF SCOPE for music21 validation and need bespoke tests.
gotchas: music21 has NO neume-shape vocabulary. It cannot tell punctum from virga from quilisma, knows nothing about ligatures, episema, custos, mode, or psalm tones. It only sees pitches+durations+text. flutter_notemus's neume.dart NcForm enum (punctum/virga/quilisma/oriscus/stropha/liquescent...) has no music21 counterpart to validate against.

music21's MEI import explicitly does NOT support mensural or neume/chant notation (documented limitation), and MEI EXPORT is not implemented at all in music21. Do not plan any MEI-based chant validation round-trip — it will not work today.

The promised `medren` package (referenced in the volpiano module docstring as 'will move to a medren package hopefully by v7') never fully landed; there is no general medieval/neume module in music21 10.x. Volpiano is the only chant-adjacent core module and it reduces chant to staff notes.

chant21 is third-party and aging (last push 2024-09, deps target music21>=5.7.2 / PyYAML==5.3.1). It is NOT installed here and is NOT guaranteed to import under music21 10.3.0 + Python 3.13 — verify in an isolated venv before depending on it. Its strict PyYAML pin is a likely install conflict.

flutter_notemus's MusicXML exporter (staffToMusicXML) is minimal: I confirmed it emits part-list/part/measure/attributes(clef,key,time)/notes but you must verify it emits divisions, ties, tuplets, dots, rests, and backup/forward for multi-voice — if any are missing or malformed, music21 may silently drop or mis-read them, masking real bugs.

The measure-duration assertion (barDuration == highestTime) will FALSE-POSITIVE on legitimate pickup measures, cadenzas, and short final measures unless you explicitly mark/handle anacrusis (Measure.paddingLeft/paddingRight).

music21 normalizes on import (makeNotation reorganizes measures, respells accidentals, regroups beams). A 'difference' the validator reports may be music21 normalizing rather than a flutter_notemus bug — compare on semantic content (pitch class+octave, quarterLength), not raw serialization.

music21 round-trips chant only as notes-on-a-staff; even via chant21 you validate melodic pitch + text underlay + structural grouping counts, NOT engraving/glyph correctness. Square-notation rendering correctness in flutter_notemus must be covered by visual/golden tests, not music21.

result.topic: W3C Music CG "notationref" JSON format-support schema and feature taxonomy (for a flutter_notemus support file)
result.keyFindings:
PROJECT. notationref (W3C Music Notation Community Group) is a "Can I Use / MDN"-style reference mapping music-notation features to the software/formats that support them. Site: https://w3c-cg.github.io/music-notationref/ . Repo: https://github.com/w3c-cg/music-notationref (default branch `main`). Repo root: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, concepts.json, index.html, w3c.json, and a `formats/` directory. The taxonomy is Common Western Music Notation (CMN) "from a developer's perspective."

TWO FILE TYPES.
(A) concepts.json — the taxonomy. A top-level JSON ARRAY of group objects. Three node types, distinguished by a `"type"` field: "group", "subgroup", "item". Group and subgroup objects have shape {"type":"group"|"subgroup","name":"<human label>","items":[ ...children ]}. Subgroups may nest inside subgroups (e.g. Dynamics has child subgroups). Leaf nodes have shape {"type":"item","id":"<kebab-case id>","name":"<human-readable description>"}. Example item: {"type":"item","id":"event-staccato","name":"Staccato"}. There are 11 top-level groups and 852 leaf item ids total.

(B) formats/<name>.json — a per-software/format support file (THIS is what flutter_notemus produces). Shape: {"name": "<format/software name>", "infoUrl": "<url about the software>", "support": { "<concept-id>": {"level": <int>, "text": "<string>", "link": "<url-or-empty>"}, ... }}. CRITICAL: the keys of the `support` object are exactly the `id` strings from concepts.json (NOT the human names). e.g. "note-sounded-pitch", "event-staccato", "lyric-melisma", "beam-cross-staff", "tuplet-nested". The template formats/empty.json contains all ~851 ids pre-populated with {"level":3,"text":"Not implemented","link":""}.

LEVEL SEMANTICS (per README): 1 = supported, 2 = partially supported, 3 = unsupported. (The reference MNX file also uses a stray 0 for one entry — treat 1/2/3 as the contract; for flutter_notemus map supported->1, partial->2, unsupported->3.)

`text` and `link` CONVENTIONS (observed in formats/mnx.json, the canonical filled example; name="MNX", infoUrl="https://w3c.github.io/mnx/docs/", 853 entries, level distribution 1:272, 2:50, 3:530). For a FORMAT, `text` holds the encoding path (e.g. "note.pitch.step") and `link` a docs URL. For SOFTWARE like flutter_notemus, `text` should be a short note on HOW it's supported (API/class, caveats for partial) and `link` an optional URL to your source/docs (may be ""). `link` is optional/may be empty; `text` should always be filled.

THE 11 TOP-LEVEL GROUPS and their subgroups:
1. Notes — Pitches (Pitch encoding; Ottava lines; Unpitched & percussion; Pitch bends; Tuning & reference pitch); Accidentals (Standard; Combination; Quarter-tone; Microtonal systems; Non-Western; Display; Cautionary/courtesy; Chord accidental layout; Scope & cancellation rules); Ties (Basic encoding; Types; Across boundaries; In chords; Rendering/placement); Markings (Articulations; Fermatas; Breath/caesuras; Ornaments; Tremolos; Grace notes; Dynamics{Levels, Hairpins/wedges, Text-based, Display}; Slurs; Glissando/portamento; Arpeggios; Bowing/string; Harmonics; Keyboard/pedal; Fingering; Plucked-string; Harp; Wind/brass; Percussion; Vocal); Stems (Direction; Length; Display); Noteheads (Standard; Special; Shape-note; Display); Beams (Encoding; Auto grouping; Cross-boundary; Rendering; Special situations).
2. Rhythms — Note values (Standard note values: maxima..4096th); Augmentation dots; Tuplets (Common; Contents; Complex structures; Display); Proportional & spatial notation.
3. Rests — Durations; Whole & multi-measure; In tuplets; Placement; Visibility/display.
4. Measures — Clefs (G/F/C/Octave-transposing/Special/Positions); Key signatures (Standard; Non-standard; Encoding; Changes; Transposing; Display); Time signatures (Simple; Compound/complex; Alternating/interchangeable; Polymeter; Changes; Mensural; Display; Metric relationships); Barlines (Types; Spanning/grouping; Display).
5. Voices and layers — Voice encoding; Multi-voice collision avoidance; Voice display.
6. Structure — Staff lines; Repeat structures (Simple repeats; Volta brackets; Simile marks); Jumps & navigation (Segno/coda; D.C.; D.S.; Jump details); Rehearsal marks & sections; Measure numbers; System & page layout (System/page breaks, page/system layout, content/layout separation); Staff visibility & ossia; Tempo markings (Absolute; Changes; Display); Swing & rhythmic feel; Text & expressions.
7. Instruments — Instruments.
8. Metadata — Metadata (includes meta-lyricist, etc.).
9. Lyrics — Lyric encoding; Syllable-to-note alignment; Hyphens; Extender lines; Verse & section structure; Lyric placement & display; Language & special text.
10. Chord symbols — Root; Quality; Extensions; Alterations; Bass/inversions; Special; Encoding; Display; Chord diagrams; Nashville; Roman numeral; Figured bass.
11. Tablature — Staff; Tuning; Fret numbers; Rhythm; With standard notation; Left/Right-hand techniques; Bends; Harmonics; Other; Display.

CHANT / NEUME FINDING (important for the user's goal). There is NO Gregorian-chant / neume / plainchant group or item in the taxonomy. A regex over all 852 ids for chant|neume|gregor|plainchant|punctum|clivis|torculus|porrectus|virga|custos|liquescen|podatus|quilisma|scandicus|climacus returned ZERO matches. The only chant/early-music-ADJACENT concepts present are: (a) musica ficta accidental -> id "note-accidental-ficta" (name references editorial/ficta accidentals); (b) Mensural time signatures -> ids "timesig-mensural-tempus-perfectum", "timesig-mensural-tempus-imperfectum", "timesig-mensural-prolatio", "timesig-mensural-proportio", "timesig-mensural-cut"; (c) a white-mensural notehead override note under noteheads ("Filled/open override (e.g., filled half note for white mensural)"); (d) the Lyrics group, which is the main vehicle for chant text underlay: ids include lyric-melisma ("one syllable sustained across multiple notes"), lyric-extender / lyric-extender-endpoint / lyric-extender-system-break, lyric-elision (synalepha), lyric-hyphen, lyric-single-syllable, lyric-multi-syllable-per-note, lyric-on-rest, lyric-ipa, lyric-language, lyric-rtl, lyric-multiple-verses, lyric-verse-number/label, lyric-placement-above/below/between. So for a flutter_notemus file, chant-specific neume rendering has no dedicated ids to mark; document chant capability indirectly via the lyrics/melisma/ficta/mensural ids, and (optionally) raise a PR/issue proposing a chant group if flutter_notemus does real neume engraving.

SUBMISSION / LINKING WORKFLOW (README). To document software/format: copy formats/empty.json, fill in name, infoUrl, and the per-concept support entries. Levels: 1 supported, 2 partial, 3 unsupported. The web app import-arbitrary-JSON-URL feature is "coming soon"; the project plans to host a directory of publicly available format JSON files. So the deliverable is a single self-hosted JSON file (e.g. in the flutter_notemus repo) that the maintainer can link/import; it must validate against the empty.json key set (same ~851 concept ids).
actionable: Generate flutter_notemus.json by starting from the canonical key list: download https://raw.githubusercontent.com/w3c-cg/music-notationref/main/formats/empty.json (it contains every concept id pre-set to level 3). Edit only the entries flutter_notemus supports/partially supports; leave the rest at level 3. This guarantees the file validates against the current taxonomy.

Use the exact root shape: {"name":"flutter_notemus","infoUrl":"<repo or pub.dev URL>","support":{ ...851 concept-id keys... }}. Keys MUST be the concept `id` strings (e.g. note-pitch-step, event-staccato, beam-secondary, tuplet-triplet, lyric-melisma), never the human-readable names.

Map flutter_notemus statuses to level ints: supported->1, partial->2, unsupported->3. For each touched entry set `text` to a short note (e.g. the Dart class/renderer that implements it, or for partial the specific limitation) and `link` to a source/docs URL or "".

Mark the engraving features flutter_notemus actually renders with level 1/2 across these high-value ids: CMN engraving -> note-pitch-step/octave/alter, accidentals (note-accidental-sharp/flat/natural/...), note-stem-direction-*, note-notehead-* , clefs (measure-clef-type-*), key/time sigs (measure-keysig-*, measure-timesig-*), barlines. Beams -> beam-basic, beam-secondary, beam-hooks, beam-group-by-beat, beam-slope. Tuplets -> tuplet-triplet, tuplet-arbitrary, tuplet-number, tuplet-ratio, tuplet-bracket-show. Dynamics -> the p/pp/mf/f/... level ids plus hairpin-cresc/decresc. Lyrics -> lyric-text, lyric-single-syllable, lyric-hyphen, lyric-melisma, lyric-extender, lyric-multiple-verses, lyric-placement-below.

For Jianpu/numbered notation already in flutter_notemus: note that notationref has NO numbered-notation (Jianpu) group either — there is nothing to mark for it. Mention this to the maintainer if Jianpu coverage matters.

Reference the filled MNX example (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/w3c-cg/music-notationref/main/formats/mnx.json) as the style guide for how `text`/`link` are written and how many entries a serious file fills (MNX: 272 at level 1, 50 at level 2).
gotchas: The support-object KEYS are the concept `id` (kebab-case, namespaced like note-*, event-*, beam-*, tuplet-*, lyric-*, timesig-*, measure-*), NOT the human-readable `name`. Using names will silently fail to match the taxonomy.

Ids are namespaced/prefixed in non-obvious ways: articulations/ornaments/dynamics live under an `event-` prefix (e.g. event-staccato, event-non-arpeggio), pitch/notehead/stem/beam/tie under `note-` or their own prefix. Do not assume the prefix — copy ids verbatim from empty.json/concepts.json.

There is minor drift between empty.json (851 keys) and the live concepts.json (852 item ids): concepts.json has event-fermata-fullbar-rest and event-fermata-text not present in empty.json, and empty.json has rest-1024th not in concepts.json. Prefer starting from the CURRENT empty.json and re-check against concepts.json; expect ~1-2 mismatches and don't treat them as errors.

No Gregorian/chant/neume taxonomy exists at all — you cannot mark neume rendering with existing keys. Inventing custom keys would break validation and the web-app view. The correct path is a taxonomy PR, not custom keys.
Level value contract is 1/2/3, but the reference MNX file contains one entry with level 0 — do not copy that; 0 is not documented. Stick to 1/2/3.

The 'import arbitrary JSON URL' web-app feature is marked 'coming soon' in the README, so right now the maintainer links/hosts the file manually (they plan a directory of format JSON files). Deliver a stable public URL.
`infoUrl` is about the software (one URL at the root), while per-entry `link` is a per-concept docs/source URL — don't confuse the two. `link` may be empty string; `text` should not be.

The taxonomy is explicitly CMN-focused 'from a developer's perspective' and acknowledges it can't cover everything — partial/edge features of flutter_notemus (e.g. Jianpu, neumes) may have no representable id, which is expected, not a file error.
